causes.text: Saudi Aramco slashed official selling prices and announced plans to ramp up oil production after Russia refused to join further output cuts, effectively launching an oil price war.

source_info.title: Oil crashes by most since 1991 as Saudi Arabia launches price war

effects.text: Bank of America's share price plunged about 15.5% as a combination of an oil price war and escalating coronavirus fears triggered a dramatic selloff in U.S. bank stocks.

source_info.title: U.S. bank shares slammed as virus, plunging oil amp up economic fears

causal_reasoning_chain.description: After OPEC+ talks collapsed, Saudi Aramco slashed prices and pledged to increase production, triggering an international oil price war.
The ensuing oil price crash intensified fears of a global recession, which were already being stoked by the spread of COVID-19.
Investors fled risky assets; Bank of America's stock plummeted about −15.5% amid a broad sell-off in energy-exposed financials.

rationale: The oil price war represented a severe commodity shock, compounding pandemic-driven economic anxieties. As investors anticipated slower growth and credit risks, they dumped bank stocks, leading to sharp declines for institutions like Bank of America.
counterfactual_analysis: If Saudi Aramco had maintained cooperative production cuts, oil prices likely would have remained more stable, which could have mitigated the bank stock rout and lessened Bank of America's losses.

adversarial_confounders.text: The rapid global spread of COVID-19 simultaneously undermined confidence in the economy and contributed to market turbulence.
adversarial_confounders.impact: While this confounder greatly influenced the sell-off, the abrupt oil price war served as a distinct and triggering catalyst.

details.pestel_factor: Economic - Rising rate expectations and inflation worries roiled growth stocks
details.commentary: Shifts in inflation and interest-rate expectations prompt investors to reassess the value of long-duration cash flows, hitting tech and other growth names hardest. Nvidia's dramatic rally left it especially sensitive to macro repricing, so even a modest change in rate expectations translated into outsized share price swings.

Once selling started in crowded AI trades, each downtick in Nvidia intensified risk management pressures and momentum-driven flows. That feedback loop between price action, positioning and sentiment magnified the impact of macro signals, producing the sharp drawdowns seen in the stock.
